findings.claim: The Task 7 slice check treats 'no ApplicationAvailability bean' as proof of the web-layer slice. Critic mutant on the overlay: a full-context test (Spring Boot test annotation plus MockMvc auto-configuration) whose properties exclude ApplicationAvailabilityAutoConfiguration and allow bean-definition overriding, with the nested fake overriding the real service bean, passes all 12 tests. The plausible full-context routes fail (full context with the fake overriding the real service; full context with a primary fake beside it; a Mockito bean in place of the fake), so this is a deliberate exclusion aimed at the shipped check, not a cheaper learner edit. README line 123 and the lab-run.json testScope state the slice claim without this residual.
findings.recommendation: Record the residual (an auto-configuration exclusion aimed at the check defeats it) in the README sentence at line 123 or in lab-run.json testScope, or accept it in reconciliation; no behavioral marker is immune to a learner who edits the context to match it.

findings.claim: Two Troubleshooting rows no longer match the shipped checks. Line 193 says ErrorSliceTest fails when 'the fake is declared outside this test class'; since the declaring-class reflection check was removed, a fake declared in a separate top-level test configuration file and imported into the slice passes all 12 tests (critic mutant on the overlay). Line 191 bolds the message 'the call to create must still be recorded', but the shipped message at WebLayerTest line 77 now reads 'the controller's create call with the posted booking must remain recorded' (critic reset mutant output), so a learner searching for the quoted text does not find it.
findings.recommendation: In the line 193 row, drop the 'declared outside this test class' clause and name the current failure causes (full application context; a Mockito mock; a fake that finds booking 1, such as an empty subclass). In the line 191 row, quote the current message text.

findings.claim: expected/test-summary.txt says the fixed GET /bookings/0 answers 'a problem+json object with the title and detail you predicted'. The prediction is no longer compared with the body: a critic mutant on the overlay with both predicted constants set to wrong non-blank text passes all 12 tests. A learner with a wrong prediction would see a body that does not match this line after a fully green run.
findings.recommendation: Say 'a problem+json object with status 400, a title and a detail: compare them with your Task 5 prediction'.

findings.claim: The standard applied to problemdetail#o2 (do not claim an objective whose half has no executable check) is not applied to three claims carried from main. bean-validation-on-requests#o2 ('Predict the status code and which fields fail for a given invalid request body'): no test takes a learner prediction; README Task 1 and Task 7 step 4 state the status, title and fields. global-error-handling#o3 ('... never expose stack traces ... while logging them on the server'): Task 2 proves the 500 becomes a 404 problem body, but nothing asks for or checks server-side logging. standard-error-responses-with-problemdetail#o1 ('... setting type, title, status, detail and an extra property'): Tasks 2 and 3 set title, status and detail only; no task or test sets type or an extra property. These claims predate this branch and were not raised by earlier loops.
findings.recommendation: Either record these partial halves in module.json sourceCoverageNotes next to the o2 gap note, or drop bean-validation-on-requests#o2 and add a small type/extra-property step plus check to Task 2 for problemdetail#o1; the reconciler may also accept them as residuals because they predate this delivery.

Loop-6 critic runs at e838bbe7 (lab bytes identical at 59ddf927) on fresh git-archive copies, JDK 25.0.5, Maven 3.9.16 offline with a private m2 copy: the starter fails exactly the 12 declared failingTests (12 run) and the private overlay regenerated for these bytes passes 12/12 with no output, twice. Reopened: the removal of the parameter-annotation reflection check leaves bean-validation-on-requests#o3 with no enforcing test. Critic mutants on the overlay with the constraint removed and a hand-written id check in byId: throwing ResponseStatusException(BAD_REQUEST) with a reason string passes all 12; throwing ErrorResponseException with a ProblemDetail detail passes all 12. Only the reason-less variant (the original loop-1 mutant) fails, in BugReportTest task5PredictsTheProblemBodyOfTheFix on the missing $.detail, so the author's claim that BugReportTest catches a hand-written check holds for that variant only. Behavioral remedy verified by the critic in work-dir copies: in task5RejectsANonPositiveIdWith400, keep the /bookings/0 MvcResult and assert getResolvedException() is a HandlerMethodValidationException (runtime exception type, not declaration shape). Results: overlay plus remedy 12/12; @Min(1) instead of @Positive plus remedy 12/12; both hand-check mutants plus remedy fail task5 with the actual exception type. Doc text hashes are of the full sentences after stripping HTML tags, unescaping entities and collapsing whitespace to single spaces (quotes below are elided). Spring Framework reference, Controllers > Validation (https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/web/webmvc/mvc-controller/ann-validation.html, retrieved 2026-11-18T13:08:54Z): 'Java Bean Validation is applied to the method when @Constraint annotations ... are declared directly on method parameters ...' (text sha256 ecc07da372713debbc8fca9eef5003b1023e5b5768aad75eeede3539fd77f3cc) and 'HandlerMethodValidationException is the exception raised validation is applied to the method.' (text sha256 635ff5cf3c41f34a9d1a2b0ef7ac5974439743bceb3543233768b51b99522e8d); Error Responses page (https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/web/webmvc/mvc-ann-rest-exceptions.html, same retrieval): ResponseEntityExceptionHandler 'handles all Spring MVC exceptions, and any ErrorResponseException' (text sha256 68f2e673786f8c9392433ef5dbd6edbe9a142ee3c1bd7cdd691459cfb94f3311), which is why the hand-written exceptions also yield a 400 problem+json once Task 6 is on. The README names the exception's page without naming its type, so asserting the type discloses neither the predicted title nor detail.
